key_insight: An efficient SHAP algorithm adapted to covariate-informed Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) makes feature-level attributions scalable for load forecasting, turning black-box foundation models into practically explainable tools for energy systems.
problem_solved: TSFMs offer strong forecasting performance but are opaque and computationally expensive to explain; this work addresses the need for fast, reliable feature attributions for critical infrastructure (power grids) so operators can trust and audit forecasts.
method: Design a SHAP-computation algorithm tailored to TSFMs that exploits model structure and covariate conditioning to reduce redundancy and compute cost.

Use approximation strategies (e.g., conditional sampling, caching of intermediate model outputs, and linearized/attention-aware decomposition) to produce accurate Shapley value estimates with far fewer model evaluations.
Evaluate the approach on covariate-informed load forecasting tasks to demonstrate scalability and fidelity vs. baseline explanation methods.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy high-performance TSFMs in energy applications with actionable, interpretable attributions—improving trust, debugging, and regulatory compliance while keeping compute costs practical for production.

paper_title: Explainable Load Forecasting with Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
paper_authors: Matthias Hertel, Alexandra Nikoltchovska, Sebastian Pütz, Ralf Mikut, Benjamin Schäfer
